page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and provides an 11 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in compute-intensive tasks. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2176.0 and a multi-core score of 19330.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 69241.15. It demonstrates top-tier performance in image processing and small-model LLM text generation. Memory bandwidth is strong for read operations, reaching 3838.93 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 193.31 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though write bandwidth is average at 77.53 GB/sec.

Built on the c8i-flex family, this instance offers a cost-efficient alternative within the compute-optimized tier by balancing high-density processing resources with a moderate memory footprint. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for heavy storage-bound or hardware-accelerated graphics workloads. However, its robust CPU instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, makes it highly effective for workloads such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based LLM inference.
